rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Gardens of Eden” is an appositive explaining the preceding “degrees.”
rows.anchor: بدل من الدرجات

words: تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rivers flow beneath the gardens, where their inhabitants remain forever.
rows.anchor: تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who purifies himself here is one who leaves polytheism by professing that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: تطهر من الشرك بقوله لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes these three verses as the two magicians’ statement.
rows.anchor: قيل هذه الآيات الثلاث حكاية قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers reading the three verses as God’s direct statement rather than a quotation of the magicians.
rows.anchor: قيل خبر من الله تعالى لا على وجه الحكاية وهو أظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted above conjectures, limits of human understanding, likeness to people, and resemblance to bodies.
rows.anchor: ارتفع عن فنون الظنون وأوهام الأفهام وتنزه عن مضاهاة الأنام ومشابهة الاجسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is the King on whom kings themselves depend.
rows.anchor: ﴾ الذي يحتاج إليه الملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The True” means that God is truly worthy of divinity.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الحق ﴾ المحق في الالوهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning the Quran and its revelation, the passage briefly digresses to instruct the Prophet about receiving it.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر القرآن وانزاله قال استطرادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Gabriel teaches the revelation, the Prophet should wait until he has heard and understood it.
rows.anchor: فتأن عليك ريثما يسمعك ويفهمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here, not rushing with the Quran means not rushing to recite it.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولا تعجل بالقرآن ﴾ بقراءته

words: مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to wait until Gabriel finishes delivering the revelation.
rows.anchor: من قبل أن يفرغ جبريل من الابلاغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks for increased knowledge of the Quran and its meanings.
rows.anchor: بالقرآن ومعانيه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported maxim says God commanded His Messenger to seek increase in nothing except knowledge.
rows.anchor: قيل ما أمر الله رسوله بطلب الزيادة في شيء إلا في العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s covenant with Adam was a revelation and command not to eat from the tree.
rows.anchor: أي أوحينا اليه أن لا يأكل من الشجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, a king’s order or counsel may be described as his advancing a command to someone or making a covenant with him.
rows.anchor: يقال في أوامر الملوك ووصاياهم تقدم الملك إلى فلان وأوصى إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam’s story is joined to the preceding warnings; the oath stresses that God commanded their forefather not to approach the tree.
rows.anchor: فعطف قصة آدم على وصرفنا فيه من الوعيد والمعنى واقسم قسما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Before” means before Adam’s descendants existed; Adam violated the prohibition just as they would, making this a rooted pattern in human conduct.
rows.anchor: من قبل وجودهم فخالف إلى ما نهى عنه كما أنهم يخالفون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He forgot the covenant, meaning the prohibition.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فنسي ﴾ العهد أي النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets are accountable for forgetfulness they could have prevented by taking care to remember.
rows.anchor: والانبياء عليهم السلام يؤاخذون بالنسيان الذي لو تكلفوا لحفظوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that Adam did not deliberately intend to defy God’s command.
rows.anchor: قصدا إلى الخلاف لأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes the phrase to mean that Adam was not among the people of firm resolve.
rows.anchor: أو لم يكن آدم من أولي العزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We found” may mean “we knew,” with “for him” and “resolve” as its two objects; or it may mean “exist,” with “for him” attached to the verb.
rows.anchor: والوجود بمعنى العلم ومفعولاه له عزما أو بمعنى نقيض العدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is Adam and his wife’s enemy because he did not prostrate and did not accept Adam.
rows.anchor: حين لم يسجد ولم يرفضك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning means Satan must not become the cause of their expulsion from the Garden.
rows.anchor: فلا يكون سببا لاحراجكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular “you suffer” fits the verse endings; it may also make the wife implicit, since the man provides for her.
rows.anchor: ولم يعل فتشقيا سراعاه لرؤس الاى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suffering is the toil of seeking the means to live.
rows.anchor: فتتعب فى طلب الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Adam was sent down with a red ox, plowed with it, and wiped sweat from his brow.
rows.anchor: وروى أنه اهبط إلى أدم ثور احمر وكان يحرث عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Therein” refers to the Garden.
rows.anchor: فى الجنه

words: إِنَّ لَكَ أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلَا تَعْرَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam would neither hunger nor lack clothing because garments are always provided in the Garden.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولا تعرى ﴾ عن الملابس لانها معده ابدا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi and Abu Bakr read “and that you” with kasra, linking it to the preceding “that”; other readers use fatḥa, linking it to “that you do not hunger.”
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإنك ﴾ بالكسر نافع وابو بكر عطفا على ان الآولى وغيرهما بالفتح عطفا على أن لا تجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no thirst in the Garden because drinks are available.
rows.anchor: لا تعطش لوجود الاشربه فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam is not exposed to the sun’s heat because the Garden has no sun and its inhabitants have extended shade.
rows.anchor: لا يصيبك حر الشمس إذ ليس فيها شمس فاهلها فى ظل ممدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two addressed are Adam and Eve.
rows.anchor: يعنى أدم وحواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enmity is among Adam’s descendants, through worldly envy and disagreement in religion.
rows.anchor: عدو بالتحاسد فى الدنيا والاختلاف فى الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance sent by God is a revealed book and religious law.
rows.anchor: كتاب وشريعا

words: فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following God’s guidance prevents worldly error and misery in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فمن اتبع هداي فلا يضل ﴾ فى الدنيا ﴿ ولا يشقى ﴾ في العقبى

words: فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God guarantees Quran followers will not stray in this life or suffer in the next.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما ضمن الله لمن اتبع القرأن الا يضل فى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who follows God’s Book, obeys its commands, and avoids its prohibitions escapes both misguidance and punishment.
rows.anchor: فمن اتبع كتاب الله وامتثل أوامره وانتهى عن نواهية نجا من الضلال ومن عقابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “My remembrance” means the Quran.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ومن أعرض عن ذكري ﴾ عن القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A constricted life” means a narrow life; the verbal noun can describe either masculine or feminine nouns.
rows.anchor: ضيقا وهو مصدر يستوى فى الوصف به المذكر والمونث

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr says the person is deprived of contentment and never feels satisfied; submission, contentment, and reliance on God make life good, while turning away brings greed and misery.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جبير يسلبه القناعه حتى لا يشبع

rows.speaker: بعض المتصوفة
rows.claim: A Sufi saying holds that turning away from remembrance darkens one’s time and unsettles one’s livelihood.
rows.anchor: كما قال بعض المتصوفة لا يعرض أحدكم عن ذكر ربه إلا أظلم عليه وقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the person is blind to proof.
rows.anchor: أعمى ﴾ من الحجة عن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the blindness as loss of physical sight.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أعمى البصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers physical blindness, comparing it with the statement that people will be gathered on their faces blind.
rows.anchor: وهو كقوله ونحشرهم يوم القيامة على وجوههم عميا وهو الوجه

words: لِمَ حَشَرْتَنِىٓ أَعْمَىٰ وَقَدْ كُنتُ بَصِيرًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrected person asks why God gathered him blind when he had sight in worldly life.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى وقد كنت بصيرا ﴾ في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Thus” means that the person acted in the same way.
rows.anchor: أي مثل ذلك فعلت أنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s clear signs came, but the person failed to consider them and turned away as though blind to them.
rows.anchor: أتتك آياتنا واضحة فلم تنظر إليها بعين المعتبر وتركتها وعميت عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise, on this Day God leaves the person to his deeds and does not lift the covering from his eyes.
rows.anchor: فكذلك اليو نتركك على عمالك ولا يزيل غطاءه عن عينيك

words: وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى مَنْ أَسْرَفَ وَلَمْ يُؤْمِنۢ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is how God repays those who transgress and disbelieve His signs.
rows.anchor: وكذلك نجزي من أسرف ولم يؤمن بآيات ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After warning of constricted life and blind resurrection, the passage concludes that the lasting Hereafter punishment is harsher than temporary hardship in life.
rows.anchor: لما توعد المعرض عن ذكره بعقوبتين المعيشة الضنك في الدنيا وحشره أعمى في العقبى

words: وَقَالُوا۟ لَوْلَا يَأْتِينَا بِـَٔايَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦٓ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers are disbelievers demanding that Muhammad bring a sign from his Lord to prove his prophethood.
rows.anchor: ﴾ أي الكافرون ﴿ لولا يأتينا بآية من ربه ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madani, Hafs, and Basri read “has it not come to them”; other readers read “have they not come to them.”
rows.anchor: / أو لم يأتهم / أو لم تأتهم مدني وحفص وبصري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In reply to their obstinate demand, the Quran itself is presented as the clearest sign and greatest miracle: it verifies earlier revealed books, which depend on its testimony because they are not miracles themselves.
rows.anchor: يعني أنهم اقترحوا على عادتهم في التعنت آية على النبوة فقيل لهم أو لم أنكم آية هي أم الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each side—Messenger and opponents—is awaiting what its outcome will be.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قل كل ﴾ أي كل واحد منا ومنكم ﴿ متربص ﴾ منتظر للعقابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to wait is addressed to the opponents.
rows.anchor: ﴿ متربص ﴾ منتظر للعقابة ولما يؤل اليه أمرنا وامركم ﴿ فتربصوا ﴾ أنتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Resurrection they will learn who follows the sound path and is guided to everlasting bliss.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فستعلمون ﴾ إذا جاءت القيامة ﴿ من أصحاب ﴾ مبتدا وخبر ومحلهما نصب

words: مَنْ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ ٱلسَّوِىِّ وَمَنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two clauses “who are the people of the path” and “who is guided” are subjects with predicates, and together occupy the accusative position.
rows.anchor: ﴿ من أصحاب ﴾ مبتدا وخبر ومحلهما نصب ﴿ الصراط السوي ﴾ المستقيم ﴿ ومن اهتدى ﴾

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report from the Messenger says that the people of Paradise recite only Sūrat Ṭā Hā and Yā Sīn; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يقرأ أهل الجنة إلى سورة طه ويس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He records the sūra’s length as 112 verses in the Kufan count and 111 in the Madinan and Basran counts.
rows.anchor: سورة الانبياء وهي مائة واثنتا عشرة آية كوفي واحدى عشرة آية مدني وبصري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is kept in its place from falling, as God says that He holds it from falling to earth except by His leave.
rows.anchor: في موضعه عن السقوط كما قال ويمسك السماء أن تقع على الأرض بإذنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the sky is guarded from devils by flaming projectiles, as another verse says.
rows.anchor: أو محفوظا بالهشب عن الشياطين كام قال وحفظناها من كل شيطان رجيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They” refers to the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وهم ﴾ أي الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs in the sky include the sun, moon, and stars; the disbelievers turn away without reflecting and believing.
rows.anchor: عن الادلة التي فها كالشمس والقمر والنجوم ﴿ معرضون ﴾ غير متفكرين فيها فيؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is for rest and day for activity.
rows.anchor: خلق الليل ﴾ لتسكنوا فيه ﴿ والنهار ﴾ لتتصرفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun serves as the day’s lamp and the moon as the night’s lamp.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والشمس ﴾ لتكون سراج النهار ﴿ والقمر ﴾ ليكون سراج الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tanwīn in “each” replaces an omitted genitive complement; it means all of them, and the pronoun refers to the sun and moon as classes of celestial bodies.
rows.anchor: التنوين فيه عوض عن المضاف إليه أي كلهم والضمير للشمس والقمر المراد بهما جنس الطوالع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the falak is the sky.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما الفلك السماء

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority say the falak is an enclosed wave beneath the sky in which the sun, moon, and stars travel.
rows.anchor: والجمور على أن الفلك موج مكفوف تحت السماء تجري فيه الشمس والقمر والنجوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They swim” means that they travel and revolve.
rows.anchor: يسيرون أي يدورون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause “they swim” is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause describing the sun and moon.
rows.anchor: والجملة في محل النصب على الحال من الشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham speaks here to make an argument against his people.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قال ﴾ محتجا عليهم

words: مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمْ شَيْـًۭٔا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Anything” is a verbal noun meaning “benefit”; the idols neither benefit nor harm those who do not worship them.
rows.anchor: ما لا ينفعكم شيئا ﴾ هو في موضع المصدر أي نفعا ﴿ ولا يضركم ﴾ أن لم تعبدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The man of the fish” means the companion of the whale; nūn is a word for whale.
rows.anchor: أي اذكر صاحب الحوت والنون الحوت فأضيف اليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Angry” means that Jonah left in opposition to his people, provoking them by departing because he feared punishment would come upon them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إذ ذهب مغاضبا ﴾ حال أي مراغما لقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Jonah grew frustrated because his people rejected his repeated reminders and persisted in disbelief, so he left in defiance.
rows.anchor: روى أنه برم بقومه لطول ما ذكرهم فلم يتعظوا وأقاموا على كفرهم فراغمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah thought departure was permissible because he acted from anger for God and hatred of disbelief, but he should have remained patient until God permitted him to migrate; he was tested in the whale’s belly.
rows.anchor: وظن أن ذلك يسوغ حيث لم يفعله الا غضبا لله وبغضا للكفر وأهله وكان عليه ان يصابروا وينتظر الاذن من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We would not constrain him” is the meaning of the phrase, rather than “We would not have power over him.”
rows.anchor: ﴿ فظن أن لن نقدر ﴾ نضيق ﴿ عليه ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In an exchange with Muawiya about the verse, Ibn Abbas distinguishes qadar, constraint, from qudra, power.
rows.anchor: وعنى ابن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه دخل يوما على معاوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The darkness may be the intense darkness inside the whale, or the combined darkness of night, sea, and whale.
rows.anchor: في بطن الحوت كقوله ذهب الله بنورهم وتركهم في ظلمات أو ظلمة الليل والبحر بطن الحوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “An” may mean “that,” or it may introduce an explanation equivalent to “that is.”
rows.anchor: أو بمعنى أي ﴿ سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين ﴾ لنفسي في خروجي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah admits he wronged himself by leaving his people before God gave permission.
rows.anchor: لنفسى في خروجي من قومي قبل ان تأذن لي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says no distressed person who calls upon God with this supplication fails to receive a response; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: في الحديث ما من مكروب يدعو بهذا الدعاء الا استجيب له

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says God saved Jonah only because he acknowledged his own wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن ما نجاه ا لله الا باقراره على نفسه بالظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Zabur is the Book given to David.
rows.anchor: كتاب داود عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first reading, “the Reminder” is the Torah.
rows.anchor: ﴿ من بعد الذكر ﴾ التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first interpretation, the land is Syria, and its heirs are Muhammad’s community.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إن الأرض ﴾ أي الشام ﴿ يرثها عبادي ﴾ ساكنة الياء حمزة غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza reads the final yāʾ in “My servants” as still; other readers give it fatḥa.
rows.anchor: ساكنة الياء حمزة غيره بفتح الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Zabur means written scripture generally, while “the Reminder” is the Preserved Tablet from which all scriptures derive.
rows.anchor: أو الزبور بمعنى المزبور أي المكتوب يعني ما أنزال على الأنبياء من الكتب والذكر أم الكتاب يعني اللوح

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza and Khalaf read the plural zubur, meaning written scriptures.
rows.anchor: قراءة حمزة وخلف بضم الزاي على جمع الزبر بمعنى المزبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the alternative interpretation, the land is the Garden.
rows.anchor: والأرض أرض الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pilgrim crosses the earth in stages, but seeing the House only deepens longing; touching the Stone does not satisfy it, and yearning sends him circling back.
rows.anchor: جعل يقطع مناكب الأرض مراحل ويتخذ مسالك المهالك منازل فاذا عاين البيت لم يزده التسلى به الا اشتياقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He presents the three obligatory rites of Hajj as a spiritual journey: ihram binds one to Islam, while standing at Arafat expresses supplication and detachment from reliance on deeds and spiritual states.
rows.anchor: وطواف الزيارة آخره فرائض الحج الثلاث وأولها الاحرام وهو عقد الالتزام يشبه الاعتصام بعروة الاسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” has an omitted predicate: either “the matter is that” or “let them do that.”
rows.anchor: خبر مبتدأ محذوف أى الأمر ذلك أو تقديره ليفعلوا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sacred inviolability is anything that may not be violated; this can mean all divine obligations or specifically the rites of Hajj.
rows.anchor: الحرمة ما لا يحل هنكه وجميع ما كلفه الله عز وجل بهذه الصفة من مناسك الحج وغيرهما فيحتمل أن يكون عاما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported interpretation identifies God’s sacred things as the Sacred House, Sacred Site, sacred month, sacred land, and Sacred Mosque.
rows.anchor: وقيل حرمات الله البيت الحرام والمشعر الحرام والشهر الحرام والبلد الحرام والمسجد الحرام

words: وَمَن يُعَظِّمْ حُرُمَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌۭ لَّهُۥ عِندَ رَبِّهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Venerating God’s sacred things is better for the person before his Lord; veneration means recognizing that they must be observed and preserved.
rows.anchor: ومعنى التعظيم العلم بأنها واجبة المراعاة والحفظ والقيام بمراعاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All livestock are lawful except what the Quran specifically excludes; people must respect its limits, neither banning lawful animals as with the bahīra nor permitting carrion or animals killed by strangling.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إلا ما يتلى عليكم ﴾ آية تحريمه وذلك قوله حرمت عليكم الميتة الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to avoid idols and false speech follows the exhortation to honor God’s sacred things because these are among the gravest violations.
rows.anchor: ولما حث على تعظيم حرماته أتبعه الامر باجتناب الاوثان وقول الزور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From idols” explains the otherwise unspecified “abomination,” as if the text said to avoid the abomination that is idols.
rows.anchor: ومن الاوثان بيان للرجس مبهم يتناول غير شئ كانه قيل فاجتنبوا الرجس الذى هو الاوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols are called an abomination by comparison: people naturally recoil from filth and should recoil from idols in the same way.
rows.anchor: وسمى الأوثان رجسا على طريقة التشبيه يعنى أنكم تنفرون بطباعكم عن الرجس فعليكم أن تنفروا عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: False speech may mean lies and slander or false testimony; shirk is also falsehood because the idolater wrongly claims an idol deserves worship.
rows.anchor: أى الكذب والبهتان أو شهادة الزور وهو من الزور وهو الانحراف لأن الشرك من باب الزور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle qad confirms an expected event; believers expected news that success would be secured for them, and the wording confirms it.
rows.anchor: قد نقضية لما هى تثبت المتوقع ولما تنفيه وكان المؤمنين يتوقعون مثل هذه البشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Success is attaining what one seeks and escaping what one fears.
rows.anchor: والفلاح الظفر بالمطلوب والنجاة من المرهوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, faith means assent, and a believer is one who assents.
rows.anchor: والإيمان فى اللغة التصديق والمؤمن المصدق لغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In religious usage, a believer is one who voices both testimonies while his heart agrees with his tongue.
rows.anchor: وفى الشرع كل من نطق بالشهادتين موطئا قلبه لسانه فهو مؤمن

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report says God commanded Paradise to speak; it declared believers successful three times and said it is forbidden to every miser and show-off, since showiness nullifies bodily worship and the person has no financial worship.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام خلق الله الجنة فقال لها تكلمى فقالت قد أفلح المؤمنون ثلاثا أنا حرام على كل بخيل مراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humility in prayer is fear in the heart and stillness in the limbs.
rows.anchor: خائفون بالقلب ساكنون بالجوارح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is to focus fully on prayer and turn away from everything else, keeping the gaze on the place of prostration and avoiding distraction or fidgeting.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون ﴾ خائفون بالقلب ساكنون بالجوارح وقيل

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda defines humility as sincere speech, reverence for the standing, complete certainty, and gathered attention.
rows.anchor: وعن أبى الدرداء هواخلاص المقال وإعظام المقام واليقين التام وجمع الاهتمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is attributed to its performers because they alone benefit from it; it is their provision and treasure, while the One worshipped has no need of it.
rows.anchor: وأضيفت الصلاة إلى المصلين لا إلى المصلى له لانتفاع المصلى بها وحده وهى عدته وذخيرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They perform zakat, and the wording “doers” suggests continuing practice more clearly than “payers.”
rows.anchor: مؤدون وبفظ فاعلون يدل على المداومة بخلاف مؤدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakat can mean the payment itself or the act of purification; the latter is intended, with the performers named for doing it.
rows.anchor: وقيل الزكاة اسم مشترك يطلق على العين وهو القدر الذى يخرجه المزكى من النصاب إلى الفقير وعلى المعنى وهو فعل المزكى الذى هو التزكية وهو المراد هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, zakat means the payment, with “performance” omitted; the preceding object takes a lām because the active participle has weaker verbal force.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالزكاة العين ويقدر مضاف محذوف وهو الاداء ودخل اللام لتقدم المفعول وضعف اسم الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccan and Sahl read the word in the singular, “their trust”; others read the plural, “their trusts.”
rows.anchor: لأمانتهم وعهدهم لأمانتهم مكى وسهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entrusted object and the matter pledged are themselves called a trust and a covenant; God’s command to return trusts to their owners illustrates the usage.
rows.anchor: سمى الشئ المؤتمن عليه والمعاهد عليه أمانة وعهدا ومنه قوله تعالى ان الله يأمركم أن تؤدوا الأمانات إلى أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording covers every trust and covenant undertaken toward God or toward other people.
rows.anchor: والمراد به العموم فى كل ما ائتمنوا عليه وعوهدوا من جهة الله عز وجل ومن جهة الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardians preserve what is entrusted; a shepherd safeguards and tends what is in his care.
rows.anchor: حافظون والراعى القائم على الشئ بحفظ وإصلاح كراعى الغنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We brought into being” means “We created.”
rows.anchor: ﴿ ثم أنشأنا ﴾ خلقنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “After them” means after Noah’s people; the new generation was ʿĀd, the people of Hud.
rows.anchor: ﴿ من بعدهم ﴾ من بعد قوم نوح ﴿ قرنا آخرين ﴾ هم عاد وقوم هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud’s statement that God made his people successors after Noah supports the identification; the stories of Hud follow Noah’s in al-Aʿraf, Hud, and al-Shuʿaraʾ.
rows.anchor: ويشهد له قول هود واذكروا إذ جعلكم خلفاء من بعد قوم نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elite speaking are from Hud’s people, and their speech answers his call.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وقال الملأ من قومه ﴾ ذكر مقالة قوم هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Aʿraf and Hud, “they said” lacks a conjunction because an imagined question prompts the answer; here wāw coordinates their words with the Messenger’s, presenting truth and falsehood together rather than a direct reply. Noah’s story uses fa because the elite’s speech immediately answers what preceded.
rows.anchor: فى الاعراف وهود بغير واو لأنه على تقدير سؤال سائل قال فما قومه فقيل له قالوا كيت وكيت وههنا مع الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Who disbelieved” may describe the elite or the whole people.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الذين كفروا ﴾ صفة للملأ أولقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They denied the encounter with everything in the Hereafter, including reckoning, reward, and punishment.
rows.anchor: أى بلقاء ما فيها من الحساب والثواب والعقاب وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made them prosperous in worldly life with abundant wealth and children.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأترفناهم ﴾ ونعمناهم ﴿ في الحياة الدنيا ﴾ بكثرة الاموال والأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “This” refers to the Prophet; they argue that he cannot claim God’s message because he is a human like them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ما هذا ﴾ أى النبى ﴿ إلا بشر مثلكم

words: يَأْكُلُ مِمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ مِنْهُ وَيَشْرَبُ مِمَّا تَشْرَبُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second “from it” is omitted after “drinks from what you drink,” since the preceding wording makes it understood.
rows.anchor: أى منه فحذف لدلالة ما قبله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi, Hamza, Ali, and Hafs read “you die” with kasra; the other readers use ḍamma.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أيعدكم أنكم إذا متم ﴾ بالكسر نافع وحمزة وعلى حفص وغيرهم بالضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are being promised resurrection for questioning, reckoning, reward, and punishment.
rows.anchor: مبعوثون للسؤال والحساب والثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating “that you” adds emphasis; the intervening time phrase makes the repetition acceptable.
rows.anchor: وثنى انكم للتأكيد وحسن ذلك للفصل بين الأول والثانى بالظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Brought forth” predicates the first “that you”; the sense is “Does he promise that you will be brought forth when you have died and become dust and bones?”
rows.anchor: ومخرجون خبر عن الأول والتقدير أيعدكم أنكم مخرجون إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “it” has no clear referent until the following phrase explains it; it originally stood for “life.”
rows.anchor: هذا ضمير لا يعلم ما يعنى به غلا بما يتلوه من بيانه وأصله ان الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers claim there is no life except the worldly life they experience.
rows.anchor: والمعنى لا حياة إلا هذه الحياة التى نحن فيها ودنت منا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative particle in enters upon a pronoun denoting the genus of life, so the construction has the force of lā negating the genus.
rows.anchor: لأن ان النافية دخلت على هى التى فى معنى الحياة الدالة على الجنس فنفتها فوازنت لا التى لنفى الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean that some die and others are born, one generation replaced by another.
rows.anchor: أى يموت بعض ويولد بعض ينقوض قرن فيأتى قرن آخر

rows.speaker: أبي وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ubayy and Ibn Masud read the phrase in reversed order, “we live and die.”
rows.anchor: أو فيه تقديم وتأخير أى نحيا ونموت وهو قراءة ابى وابن مسعود رضى الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deny being raised after death.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وما نحن بمبعوثين ﴾ بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel’s cry struck them and destroyed them.
rows.anchor: أى صيحة جبريل صاح عليهم فدمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In truth” means justly, as when one says someone judges by the truth, meaning justice.
rows.anchor: بالعدل من الله يقال فلان يقضى بالحق أى بالعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their destruction is likened to flood debris: decayed, blackened leaves and twigs carried by a torrent.
rows.anchor: شبههم فى دمارهم بالغثاء وهو حميل السيل مما بلى واسود من الورق والعيدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buʿdan means destruction; it is a verbal noun used with an unexpressed verb that is not used explicitly.
rows.anchor: فهلاكا يقال بعد بعدا وأبعد هلك وهو من المصادر المنصوبة بافعال لا يستعمل اظهارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “For the wrongdoing people” identifies those cursed with destruction, like the phrase hīt laka.
rows.anchor: ﴿ للقوم الظالمين ﴾ بيان لمن دعى عليه بالبعد نحو هيت لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The Truth” refers to God.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولو اتبع الحق ﴾ أى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God followed their desires concerning the gods they believe in, the heavens, earth, and their inhabitants would be corrupted.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أهواءهم ﴾ فيما يعتقدون من الآلهة ﴿ لفسدت السماوات ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He supports this argument with the verse saying that if there were gods besides God in heaven and earth, both would be corrupted.
rows.anchor: كما قال لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rational beings are singled out because everything else follows them.
rows.anchor: خص العقلاء بالذكر لأن غيرهم تبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reminder is the Book, which admonishes them and honors them because the Messenger is one of them and the Quran is in their language.
rows.anchor: بالكتاب الذى هو ذكرهم أى وعظهم أو شرفهم لأن الرسول منهم والقرآن بلغتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means the reminder they had wished for, saying, “If only we had a reminder from earlier peoples.”
rows.anchor: أو بالذكر الذى كانوا يتمنونه ويقولون لو أن عندنا ذكرا من الأولين الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their turning away from the reminder is by their own bad choice.
rows.anchor: بسوء اختيارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hijazi, Basri, and Asim read kharjan followed by kharāju; Ali and Hamza read kharjan followed by kharju; the Shami reading has kharājan followed by kharāju.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أم تسألهم خرجا فخراج ربك خير ﴾ حجازى وبصرى وعاصم خرجا فخرج على وحمزة شامى خراجا فخراج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kharaj is what one pays a ruler as land tax or a worker as wages; kharj is narrower, while kharaj is broader, as in village revenue versus Kufa’s levy.
rows.anchor: وهو ما تخرجه إلى الإمام من زكاة أرضك وإلى كل عامل من أجرته وجعله والخرج أخص من الخراج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reading is preferable because the greater length of kharaj suits its broader meaning.
rows.anchor: فزيادة اللفظ لزيادة المعنى ولذا حسنت القراءة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether the Prophet seeks even a small payment from people for guiding them, when the Creator’s ample provision is better.
rows.anchor: يعنى أم تسألهم على هدايتك لهم قليلا من عطاء الخلق فالكثير من الخالق خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the best of givers.
rows.anchor: أفضل المعطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is the religion of Islam, so the people should answer the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وهو دين الإسلام فحقيق أن يستجيبوا لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s signs here are the Quran, recited to them in worldly life; they denied it and claimed it was not from God.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ألم تكن آياتي ﴾ أى القرآن ﴿ تتلى عليكم ﴾ فى الدنيا ﴿ فكنتم بها تكذبون ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Overcame us” means “mastered us.”
rows.anchor: ﴿ قالوا ربنا غلبت علينا ﴾ ملكتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza and Ali read shaqwatunā; other readers read shaqāwatunā. Both are verbal nouns for misery.
rows.anchor: ﴿ شقوتنا ﴾ شقاوتنا حمزة وعلى وكلاهما مصدر أى شقينا بأعمالنا السيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the exegetes’ claim that a prewritten decree of misery overwhelmed them: God writes what a person does and knows he will choose, so the person is neither overpowered nor compelled.
rows.anchor: وقول أهل التأويل غلب علينا ما كتب علينا من الشقاوة لا يصح لأنه إنما يكتب ما يفعل العبد وما يعلم أنه يختاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call their own sinful deeds the cause of their misery; this is an excuse for their neglect, not grounds for absolution.
rows.anchor: وهذا لأنهم إنما يقولون ذلك القول اعتذارا لما كان منهم من التفريط فى أمره فلا يجمل أن يطلبوا لأنفسهم عذرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were astray from the truth and what is right.
rows.anchor: عن الحق والصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s steps are his traces and whispers, followed by listening to the slander and talking about it.
rows.anchor: أى آثاره ووساوسه بالاصغاء إلى الافك والقول فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fahshāʾ is what is extremely vile.
rows.anchor: ما أفرط قبحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munkar is what people’s souls reject, recoil from, and disapprove.
rows.anchor: ما تنكره النفوس فتنفر عنه ولا ترتضيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without God’s favor and mercy in granting expiatory repentance, none would have been purified of the slander’s sin thereafter.
rows.anchor: تفضل عليكم بالتوبة الممحصة لما طهر منكم أحد آخر الدهر من أثم الافك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God purifies those who repent by accepting their sincere repentance.
rows.anchor: يطهر التائبين بقبول توبتهم إذا محضوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears what people say and knows their inner selves and sincerity.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والله سميع ﴾ لقولهم ﴿ عليم ﴾ بضمائرهم وإخلاصهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In houses” may attach to the niche in the preceding parable, meaning a niche in some mosques; repeating “in them” reinforces the wording.
rows.anchor: يتعلق بمشكاة أى كمشكاة فى بعض بيوت الله وهى المساجد كأنه قيل مثل نوره كما يرى فى المسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it attaches to an omitted command: “glorify in houses.”
rows.anchor: أو بمحذوف أى سبحوا فى بيوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s permission here means His command.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أذن الله ﴾ أى أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Be raised” can mean built, as in verses about raising a structure and Abraham raising the foundations.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أن ترفع ﴾ تبنى كقوله بناها رفع سمكها فسواها وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says God commanded that the houses be honored, not built.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن ما أمر الله أن نرفع بالبناء ولكن بالتعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God’s name can mean reciting His Book or any form of remembrance.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ويذكر فيها اسمه ﴾ يتلى فيها كتابه أو هو عام فى كل ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “glorify” means pray: at dawn is the Fajr prayer, while the evening term includes Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and ʿIshāʾ; dawn is singular because it has one prayer, while evening covers several.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال ﴾ أى يصلى له فيها بالغداة صلاة الفجر وبالآصال صلاة الظهر والعصر والعشاءين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āṣāl is the plural of aṣīl, the late afternoon.
rows.anchor: والآصال جمع أصل جمع أصيل وهو العشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shami and Abu Bakr read the verb actively, making “men” its subject; the other reading is passive, with “men” raised by an understood verb.
rows.anchor: ﴿ رجال ﴾ فاعل يسبح يسبح شامى وأبو بكر ويسند إلى أحد الظروف الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the passive reading, “men” is raised by what the wording implies: “men glorify God.”
rows.anchor: ورجال مرفوع بمادل عليه يسبح أى يسبح له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that trade does not distract them.
rows.anchor: لا تشغلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trade refers to travel and sale to activity at home; alternatively, trade means buying, while sale is singled out because its profit is more certain and therefore more distracting.
rows.anchor: ﴿ تجارة ﴾ فى السفر ﴿ ولا بيع ﴾ فى الحضر وقيل التجارة الشراء اطلاقا لاسم الجنس على النوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their remembrance of God is with both tongue and heart.
rows.anchor: ﴿ عن ذكر الله ﴾ باللسان والقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ in iqāma replaces the dropped root letter; when the word is annexed, the genitive construction replaces the tāʾ.
rows.anchor: التاء فى إقامة عوض من العين الساقطة للأعلال الأصل أقوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that neither trade nor sale distracts them from giving zakat.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإيتاء الزكاة ﴾ أى وعن إيتاء الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possibility is that they do no buying or selling, like the devoted solitary; another is that they trade while remembering God and promptly rise for prayer, like the sociable devoted.
rows.anchor: والمعنى لا تجارة لهم حتى تلهيهم كأولياء العزلة أو يبيعون ويشترون ويذكرون الله مع ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Fearing a day” may be circumstantial from the pronoun in “distracts them” or another adjective describing the men.
rows.anchor: ويخافون حال من الضمير في تلهيهم أو صفة أخرى لرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearts may turn by rising to the throats and eyes by staring and turning blue; alternatively, hearts turn from disbelief to faith and eyes from denial to direct vision, as in the verse about the lifted veil.
rows.anchor: ﴿ تتقلب فيه القلوب ﴾ ببلوغها إلى الجناجر ﴿ والأبصار ﴾ بالشخوص والزرقة أو تتقلب القلوب إلى الإيمان بعد الكفران
